newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks drift to weak close ahead US data.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks drift to weak close ahead US data.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slumbered to a lower close on Friday, with investors cautiously awaiting key U.S. August jobs data due later for further clues on the direction of interest rates, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index fell 14.92 points to 11,025.59, after falling to a low of 10,930.37. Turnover was HK$3.35 billion compared to HK$3.53 billion on Thursday.

"The fact is interest rates are rearing their ugly head again and it is making investors think twice before jumping in, especially with the data coming out tonight," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"Some investors don't think it is worth the risk to be fully invested," he said.
Analysts said stronger-than-expected U.S. August payrolls were likely to trigger further weakness in stock prices next week. The Hang Seng index fell 133.43 points this week.

"It is highly possible that (stronger-than-expected data) will trigger a tumble in U.S. stocks and bonds and so that will harm the performance of the local stock market," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
Analysts said sharp falls in banking stocks early on had triggered some bargain-hunting in afternoon trade, allowing the Hang Seng index to end off its lows.
HSBC Holdings closed HK$0.50 lower at HK$131.50 after falling to a session low of HK$130.50. Hang Seng Bank slipped HK$0.25 to HK$78.00 after falling to HK$77.00.
Among the blue chips, Swire Pacific dropped HK$1.00 to HK$66.75.

"Speculation that its (Island Place) flats sale response may not be as good as expected, because the company has set the price at a relatively high level, gave investors an excuse to take profit ahead of weekend," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Chia said a move away from the blue chips had turned attention to the some second line stocks. Termbray Industries rose HK$1.60 to HK$21.60.
The H-share index added 1.94 points to 801.27.
Some property stocks advanced, with Sun Hung Kai Properties up HK$0.25 to HK$74.50 and Cheung Kong up HK$0.25 to HK$54.25. New World Development rose HK$0.10 to HK$37.30.
